fun_fact: India was once home to more than 50 mn vultures — until the 1990s, when Diclofenac, a common painkiller for cattle, but poisonous for vultures who ate the carcass, wiped out more than 99% of their population. Vultures are nature's clean-up crew, stripping carcasses before they rot. Without them, feral dog and rat populations surged and disease spread. [A BBC report](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c28e2pvzn3lo) says ~5 lac human deaths can be linked to the decline of the vulture.
